Why now

A desktop app you can technically view on a phone isn't a mobile app.

Skiffle today is a desktop web app in a mobile wrapper. It's the reason usage sits in the high teens and won't climb — dealers dip in to check one thing rather than living in the app. The clearest proof is what happens when a dealer needs a measurement mid-fitting.

Today · Skiffle web wrapper
Dealer taps Measurements, mid-fitting, client watching.
App kicks out to external Safari.
Safari demands a second WorkFlow login.
Dealer stalls the room while it loads.
↑ actual v1 build: measurements, native, same session
Who it's for

Three dealers. One core they all depend on.

v1 optimizes for Frank first — utterly reliable, dead simple, never embarrassing in front of a client — while still serving Dale and Sal. Order status plus search is the non-negotiable core all three share.

The Veteran

Frank

Pain: fumbling in front of a client, can't pull up status fast enough

Wants order status or a fabric instantly during a client call — nothing more, nothing less.

Proof point
Dashboard-first home with orders one tap away, global search, one-tap order lookup
The Closer

Dale

Pain: friction on the move that breaks the pitch

Sells on the move. Lives in the model library, collections, and fabrics, and captures new clients with photos on the fly.

Proof point
Model library, find-fabric, new-client capture with photos, and the shoulder-slope flagship
The Boutique Owner

Sal

Pain: surprise delays and losing track of production

Tracks each order's production stage, catches delays before they become a phone call, and keeps client records sharp.

Proof point
Per-garment status, inline carrier tracking with ESD, and delayed/shipped/delivered push
What's inside

Everything today's app does — plus what only native can.

v1 is parity-plus: the same information architecture dealers already know, rebuilt bottom-up for the phone, with a small native dividend spent where it earns its keep. Screens below are pulled straight from the current build.

Global search & client index

One debounced, permission-scoped search across clients, fabrics, orders, and item numbers, plus an A-to-Z jump index over roughly 1,280 clients.

Per-garment order tracking

Fabric Hold through Delivery, at the garment level — not one blunt order-level badge — with inline carrier tracking (UPS, FedEx, DHL) and a tappable ESD.

Fabric explorer & scan-to-find

Search or scan a physical fabric-folder QR code and land straight on fabric detail — spec sheet, price, and stock status included.

Tools hub

Model Library, Spec Charts, Fitting Guide, Materials, Fabric Explorer, and the permission-gated Price List — remote-updatable, no app release needed.

Dealer Rank

A rank pill on Orders opens the full report — MTD, YTD, standing among neighbors, and multi-year history. No dollar amounts shown, by dealer request.

★ fixes the 1st-of-month "N/A" bug

Push + live chat

Transactional alerts — delayed, shipped, delivered — plus a persistent Intercom chat, so support is always one tap away, never a phone call.

The moment worth screenshotting.

The garment render — swatch and model toggles — is the single frame dealers screenshot straight into a client text today. It's parity in this rebuild, and it's earned a place as the thing v1 must not lose.

Path to launch

Back-planned from the January shows.

Every industry show season is a window to debut a production launch — this schedule works backward from it. Dates hold as a shared target; an AI-assisted build may compress the middle of it.

One codebase. Two platforms. A dealer who never has to leave a room to check on an order.

Migration target: roughly 30 blended daily actives within 60 days of GA, 25% trailing-30-day stickiness within 90 days — up from about 17 and 16% today. Full detail is in the PRD and GTM plan.
